## Thinking it through

**Step 1 — What does every existing sparse method get wrong in the same way?**

Sliding-window, Quest, block-top-K all share one silent failure mode: whatever isn't selected is treated as if it *doesn't exist*. The softmax renormalizes over the survivors. Two distortions follow:

1. **Denominator lie.** In the dense model, a needle key at 8K wins attention *against* thousands of weak competitors. Drop the competitors and every surviving key's weight is inflated; the output distribution over values shifts away from what the pretrained residual stream expects. QA F1 suffers because diffuse "background evidence" mass — small per token, large in aggregate — is deleted, not approximated.

2. **Selection criterion mismatch.** Quest scores a block by a max-style upper bound (great for needles, systematically over-selects spiky junk blocks); mean-pooled scoring (great for QA-style diffuse evidence) *misses* needles, because one hot key vanishes into the block mean. Nobody's block score captures both regimes.

**Step 2 — The reframe.** Under the budget, we don't have to choose between "attend exactly" and "delete." There's a third state: **attend coarsely**. Every unselected block can be collapsed into a single *phantom token* that participates in the *same* softmax as the exact tokens. Cost: one extra slot per block, ~n/64 — statistically free against a 0.25 density budget.

**Step 3 — The crux: what logit do you give a phantom token?** The naive choice, `q·k̄_b` (attend to the block-mean key), is wrong in a precise, fixable way. We want the phantom to carry the block's *total* softmax mass: Σᵢ exp(s·q·kᵢ). Model the within-block dot products as Gaussian, q·kᵢ ~ N(q·k̄_b, q᷐Cᵦq), approximate the quadratic form isotropically with a cached scalar σ²_b = mean per-dim key variance, and the moment-generating function gives:

**ℓ_b = s·q·k̄_b + log n_b + ½·s²·σ²_b·‖q‖²**,  phantom value = v̄_b.

Three terms, three jobs: mean similarity, block size (mass conservation), and a **Jensen-gap variance correction**. That last term is the payoff:

- It makes the phantom mass a *calibrated* estimate of the dropped mass → the denominator is honest, exact-block weights match dense-model attention scale. Fixes distortion (1).
- Now use **the same ℓ_b as the block-selection score** (top-K blocks per head per query-block by ℓ_b). A block containing one needle key has huge σ²_b — the variance term flags it even though the mean hides it. A block of uniformly moderate evidence has high mean term. One scalar handles both regimes. Fixes distortion (2), replacing Quest's loose max-bound with an expected-mass criterion that is budget-optimal in the "capture the most attention mass exactly" sense.

**Step 4 — Assembly (Foveated, Mass-Conserving Sparse Attention):**

- Per forward, per KV block b: cache k̄_b, v̄_b, n_b, σ²_b — one O(n) pass.
- Per query block: exact attention over {sink block, 2 diagonal/local blocks, top-K blocks by ℓ_b} spending ~0.23 density; **concatenate phantom logits ℓ_b for all remaining causally-complete blocks** (strictly below the diagonal query block; partial block is covered by the exact local band) and their values v̄_b; run **one softmax over exact + phantom slots**. Output = exact-weighted values + phantom-weighted centroid values.
- Replays identically at every generation step (fully recomputed from q,k,v, no mutable state), so it's drift-free under the parallel-forward protocol. GQA replication is handled upstream; per-head top-K naturally lets retrieval heads and local heads pick different blocks.

Why this beats the baselines specifically here: on **niah_8k**, the variance term guarantees needle-block selection *and* the honest denominator keeps the needle's attention weight at its dense-model value rather than an inflated one (important when the model must copy the needle verbatim). On **Qasper/MultiFieldQA**, the phantom background preserves the aggregate contribution of thousands of weakly-relevant tokens that hard-sparse methods amputate — the residual stream sees an input statistically close to dense attention's, which is exactly what "no retraining" demands.

**Core idea:** Replace hard block deletion with moment-matched phantom tokens — each unselected block enters the shared softmax as one slot with logit `q·k̄_b + log n_b + ½σ²_b‖q‖²` and value v̄_b — and use that same variance-corrected expected-mass score to select which blocks get exact attention.

**Non-trivial crux:** The second-moment (Jensen-gap) correction is doing double duty: it calibrates the softmax denominator to conserve dropped attention mass, and it is the only cheap block statistic that makes a mean-pooled score needle-sensitive — unifying Quest-style spike detection and diffuse-evidence retention in a single scalar per block.

# Task: mlsys-sparse-attention-inference

# Long-Context Inference-Time Sparse Attention

## Research Question
Design a **sparse attention module** that drops into a pretrained 1.4B-param
causal LLM at inference time and preserves long-context task quality under a
fixed sparsity budget — no retraining, no fine-tuning, no architectural
surgery beyond replacing the attention forward.

## Background
Inference-time sparse attention has been studied along two axes:
**static patterns** (sliding-window, sink + window, BigBird block-sparse,
dilated) and **content-adaptive patterns** (Reformer LSH, NSA-style block-
top-K, Quest). KV-cache compression methods (H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM)
are designed for autoregressive decode with a mutable KV cache and are not
evaluated here — this benchmark uses a parallel-forward setup where every
forward processes the full prefix in one shot and the same `SparseAttention`
module replays at every generation step. Methods whose importance signal
shifts with the observation window (H2O, SnapKV) drift during generation
under this setting; we therefore restrict the baseline set to methods that
operate correctly under parallel forward.

NIAH retrieval and LongBench QA evaluations need instruction-following
ability, so this task uses an instruction-tuned backbone rather than a
base model.

The agent's `SparseAttention` instance (one per attention layer) is
monkey-patched into `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` (12 query heads, 2 KV
heads — the harness handles GQA replication so this module sees 12 heads
on both Q and K/V). Three downstream tasks exercise different long-context
capabilities:

| Env                       | Metric        | Notes                                                  |
|---------------------------|---------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| niah_8k                   | retrieval acc | Synthetic Needle-In-A-Haystack at 8K context           |
| longbench_qasper          | QA F1         | LongBench Qasper single-doc scientific paper QA        |
| longbench_multifieldqa_en | QA F1         | LongBench MultiFieldQA-EN long-document multi-field QA |

## Task
Edit the `SparseAttention` class in
`sparse-attn-eval/custom_sparse_attn.py` (lines 31-103). The rest of the
file, plus `harness.py` and `run_llm.py`, are read-only — they handle model
loading, attention monkey-patching, density tracking, and metric computation.

## Interface
```python
class SparseAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, head_dim, num_heads, block_size=64, density_budget=0.25): ...
    def forward(self, q, k, v, is_causal=False, scale=None) -> torch.Tensor: ...
```

`q`, `k`, `v` arrive as `(B, H, N, D)` in float16/bfloat16. `is_causal=True`
for the causal LLM. Return the attention output in the same shape and dtype.

After every forward, set `self.last_density` to the fraction of (q, k) pairs
that received non-zero attention (causal-adjusted: divide by `N(N+1)/2` when
`is_causal=True`). The harness aggregates `last_density` across all attention
layers and **aborts the run if the mean exceeds the density budget
(0.25 + 0.02 slack)** for any non-`dense` baseline. Missing, NaN, infinite,
negative, or >1 density reports are treated as harness errors, not as zero
density.

## Sparsity Budget
- `density_budget = 0.25`.
- Only the reference `dense` baseline is allowed to exceed it: it reports
  the true `last_density = 1.0`, and the dense run is invoked with
  `ALLOW_DENSE_FLAG=1` (set as a baseline-level env var in `config.json`)
  which forwards `--allow-dense` to `run_llm.py` so
  `harness.enforce_budget(allow_dense=True)` skips the budget check.

## Constraints
- Inference only — do **not** modify weights, do **not** add training.
- Single A100 80GB; FP16 only (no FP8).
- No Triton kernels; pure PyTorch ops or `torch.nn.attention.flex_attention`
  if available in this PyTorch version.
- Branching on `is_causal` and on `N` is fine. The forward signature includes
  `is_causal` for forward compatibility (currently always True).

## Baselines (already implemented for reference)
1. **dense** — full attention oracle (density 1.0; the only baseline allowed
   to exceed the 0.25 budget).
2. **streaming_llm** — 4 attention sinks + sliding window (Xiao et al., ICLR
   2024). Canonical static sink+window pattern.
3. **bigbird** — global + window + random block-sparse pattern (Zaheer et
   al., NeurIPS 2020). Static, theoretically full-rank.
4. **block_topk** — content-adaptive block-level top-K via mean-pooled-key
   scoring (Yuan et al., NSA 2024 — block-selection branch). Diagonal block
   always retained; importance computed per query block at inference time.

All baselines are paper-faithful and operate correctly in parallel-forward
mode (use_cache=False). H2O / SnapKV / Quest are deliberately excluded:
their importance signal is keyed off a mutable KV cache during decode and
does not transfer cleanly to single-shot prefill+generate without cache
plumbing that this harness does not implement.

A good submission should beat or match every baseline on at least two of
the three environments without overshooting the density budget.

"""Inference-time sparse attention module (agent-editable).

Single class ``SparseAttention`` is monkey-patched into Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
by the harness, which calls ``forward(q, k, v, is_causal=True, scale=...)``
once per attention layer (q/k/v already shaped (B, H, N, D), GQA replicated).
The harness reads ``self.last_density`` after every forward and aborts if
density > 0.25 (small slack), except for the dense reference baseline.

PERFORMANCE — read this before redesigning forward(). At N=8192 a naïve
``einsum + softmax + einsum`` materializes a 3 GB bf16 attention matrix per
layer per head and is *slower than dense*. To make sparse actually faster:

  1. Use fused SDPA: ``F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=
     bool_mask, ...)`` is 5–10× faster than einsum + manual softmax.
  2. Cache the mask across layers — it depends only on (N, pattern), not
     q/k/v values, so build once per prompt and reuse across all 24 layers.
  3. For low density (≤ 10%), use ``torch.nn.attention.flex_attention`` with
     ``create_block_mask`` — it compiles a true block-sparse kernel that
     skips entire blocks (PyTorch-native, no Triton-by-hand needed).
  4. Stay in bf16 — fused SDPA handles numerics safely; fp32 upcast 2×s memory.
"""

import math

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EDITABLE REGION START — design the inference-time sparse attention here.
# Lines 31-103 are agent-editable. Everything outside this region is FIXED.

class SparseAttention(nn.Module):
    """Foveated, mass-conserving block-sparse attention.

    Exact attention over {sink, local band, top-K} blocks chosen by the
    variance-corrected expected-mass score
        l_b = s*q.k_mean_b + log n_b + 0.5*s^2*sigma2_b*||q||^2 ,
    while every remaining causally-complete block enters the SAME softmax
    as one moment-matched "phantom" slot (logit l_b, value v_mean_b).
    """

    def __init__(self, head_dim, num_heads, block_size=64, density_budget=0.25):
        super().__init__()
        self.head_dim = head_dim
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.block_size = block_size
        self.density_budget = density_budget
        self.exact_budget = 0.245  # exact-block target; phantoms add ~1/64
        self.chunk = 2048          # query-row chunk (memory-bounded attention)
        self.last_density = None

    @torch.no_grad()
    def forward(self, q, k, v, is_causal=False, scale=None):
        B, H, N, D = q.shape
        Bk = self.block_size
        s = scale if scale is not None else 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)
        dev = q.device
        n_b = (N + Bk - 1) // Bk
        Npad = n_b * Bk
        pad = Npad - N
        kp = F.pad(k.float(), (0, 0, 0, pad))
        vp = F.pad(v.float(), (0, 0, 0, pad))
        qp = F.pad(q.float(), (0, 0, 0, pad))
        cnt = torch.full((n_b,), float(Bk), device=dev)
        cnt[-1] = float(N - (n_b - 1) * Bk)
        kb = kp.view(B, H, n_b, Bk, D)
        k_mean = kb.sum(3) / cnt[:, None]
        k_var = (kb.square().sum(3) / cnt[:, None] - k_mean.square()).clamp_min(0)
        sigma2 = k_var.mean(-1)                                   # (B,H,n_b)
        v_mean = (vp.view(B, H, n_b, Bk, D).sum(3) / cnt[:, None]).to(q.dtype)
        log_n = cnt.log()
        # ── block selection by pooled expected-mass score ────────────────
        qb = qp.view(B, H, n_b, Bk, D)
        q_mean = qb.sum(3) / cnt[:, None]
        q_nrm2 = qb.square().sum((3, 4)) / cnt                    # (B,H,n_b)
        sel = s * torch.einsum('bhmd,bhnd->bhmn', q_mean, k_mean)
        sel = sel + log_n.view(1, 1, 1, n_b)
        sel = sel + (0.5 * s * s * sigma2.unsqueeze(2) * q_nrm2.unsqueeze(3)).clamp_max(0.4)
        bi = torch.arange(n_b, device=dev)
        causal_blk = bi[:, None] >= bi[None, :]
        # per-row exact block count K from budget: K(2n+1-K)=b*n(n+1)
        disc = max(0.0, (2 * n_b + 1) ** 2 - 4 * self.exact_budget * n_b * (n_b + 1))
        K_top = max(1, int(((2 * n_b + 1) - math.sqrt(disc)) / 2))
        forced = torch.eye(n_b, dtype=torch.bool, device=dev)
        for d in (1, 2):
            if K_top >= d + 1 and n_b > d:
                forced |= torch.diag(torch.ones(n_b - d, dtype=torch.bool, device=dev), -d)
        if K_top >= 4: forced[:, 0] = True
        kk = max(0, min(K_top - min(K_top, 4 if n_b > 1 else 1), n_b))
        sel = sel.masked_fill(~causal_blk | forced, float('-inf'))
        keep = forced.view(1, 1, n_b, n_b).expand(B, H, n_b, n_b).clone()
        if kk > 0:
            keep.scatter_(-1, sel.topk(kk, dim=-1).indices, True)
        keep &= causal_blk
        phant = (bi[:, None] > bi[None, :]) & ~keep               # (B,H,n_b,n_b)
        # ── density accounting (phantom slot = 1 kv pair per query row) ──
        pairs = cnt[:, None] * cnt[None, :] - torch.diag(cnt * (cnt - 1) / 2.0)
        exact_pairs = (keep * pairs).sum((-1, -2))                # (B,H)
        ph_pairs = (phant.sum(-1).float() * cnt).sum(-1)          # (B,H)
        denom = N * (N + 1) / 2.0 if is_causal else float(N * N)
        self.last_density = float(((exact_pairs + ph_pairs) / denom).mean().item())
        # ── one softmax over exact tokens + phantom slots, chunked ───────
        tok = torch.arange(N, device=dev)
        kblk = tok // Bk
        km16 = k_mean.to(q.dtype)
        out = torch.empty_like(q)
        for r0 in range(0, N, self.chunk):
            r1 = min(r0 + self.chunk, N)
            qc = q[:, :, r0:r1]
            rows = tok[r0:r1]
            rb = rows // Bk
            lg = torch.matmul(qc, k.transpose(-2, -1)).float() * s
            keep_c = keep[:, :, rb, :][:, :, :, kblk]
            keep_c &= rows[:, None] >= tok[None, :]
            lg.masked_fill_(~keep_c, float('-inf'))
            qn2 = qc.float().square().sum(-1)                     # (B,H,C)
            lp = torch.matmul(qc, km16.transpose(-2, -1)).float() * s
            lp += log_n + (0.5 * s * s * sigma2.unsqueeze(2) * qn2.unsqueeze(-1)).clamp_max(0.4)
            lp.masked_fill_(~phant[:, :, rb, :], float('-inf'))
            a = torch.softmax(torch.cat([lg, lp], -1), -1)
            a = torch.nan_to_num(a, nan=0.0).to(q.dtype)
            out[:, :, r0:r1] = torch.matmul(a[..., :N], v) + torch.matmul(a[..., N:], v_mean)
        return out


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EDITABLE REGION END
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Research proposal — implement THIS idea (provided by the caller)

## Thinking it through

**Step 1 — What does every existing sparse method get wrong in the same way?**

Sliding-window, Quest, block-top-K all share one silent failure mode: whatever isn't selected is treated as if it *doesn't exist*. The softmax renormalizes over the survivors. Two distortions follow:

1. **Denominator lie.** In the dense model, a needle key at 8K wins attention *against* thousands of weak competitors. Drop the competitors and every surviving key's weight is inflated; the output distribution over values shifts away from what the pretrained residual stream expects. QA F1 suffers because diffuse "background evidence" mass — small per token, large in aggregate — is deleted, not approximated.

2. **Selection criterion mismatch.** Quest scores a block by a max-style upper bound (great for needles, systematically over-selects spiky junk blocks); mean-pooled scoring (great for QA-style diffuse evidence) *misses* needles, because one hot key vanishes into the block mean. Nobody's block score captures both regimes.

**Step 2 — The reframe.** Under the budget, we don't have to choose between "attend exactly" and "delete." There's a third state: **attend coarsely**. Every unselected block can be collapsed into a single *phantom token* that participates in the *same* softmax as the exact tokens. Cost: one extra slot per block, ~n/64 — statistically free against a 0.25 density budget.

**Step 3 — The crux: what logit do you give a phantom token?** The naive choice, `q·k̄_b` (attend to the block-mean key), is wrong in a precise, fixable way. We want the phantom to carry the block's *total* softmax mass: Σᵢ exp(s·q·kᵢ). Model the within-block dot products as Gaussian, q·kᵢ ~ N(q·k̄_b, q᷐Cᵦq), approximate the quadratic form isotropically with a cached scalar σ²_b = mean per-dim key variance, and the moment-generating function gives:

**ℓ_b = s·q·k̄_b + log n_b + ½·s²·σ²_b·‖q‖²**,  phantom value = v̄_b.

Three terms, three jobs: mean similarity, block size (mass conservation), and a **Jensen-gap variance correction**. That last term is the payoff:

- It makes the phantom mass a *calibrated* estimate of the dropped mass → the denominator is honest, exact-block weights match dense-model attention scale. Fixes distortion (1).
- Now use **the same ℓ_b as the block-selection score** (top-K blocks per head per query-block by ℓ_b). A block containing one needle key has huge σ²_b — the variance term flags it even though the mean hides it. A block of uniformly moderate evidence has high mean term. One scalar handles both regimes. Fixes distortion (2), replacing Quest's loose max-bound with an expected-mass criterion that is budget-optimal in the "capture the most attention mass exactly" sense.

**Step 4 — Assembly (Foveated, Mass-Conserving Sparse Attention):**

- Per forward, per KV block b: cache k̄_b, v̄_b, n_b, σ²_b — one O(n) pass.
- Per query block: exact attention over {sink block, 2 diagonal/local blocks, top-K blocks by ℓ_b} spending ~0.23 density; **concatenate phantom logits ℓ_b for all remaining causally-complete blocks** (strictly below the diagonal query block; partial block is covered by the exact local band) and their values v̄_b; run **one softmax over exact + phantom slots**. Output = exact-weighted values + phantom-weighted centroid values.
- Replays identically at every generation step (fully recomputed from q,k,v, no mutable state), so it's drift-free under the parallel-forward protocol. GQA replication is handled upstream; per-head top-K naturally lets retrieval heads and local heads pick different blocks.

Why this beats the baselines specifically here: on **niah_8k**, the variance term guarantees needle-block selection *and* the honest denominator keeps the needle's attention weight at its dense-model value rather than an inflated one (important when the model must copy the needle verbatim). On **Qasper/MultiFieldQA**, the phantom background preserves the aggregate contribution of thousands of weakly-relevant tokens that hard-sparse methods amputate — the residual stream sees an input statistically close to dense attention's, which is exactly what "no retraining" demands.

**Core idea:** Replace hard block deletion with moment-matched phantom tokens — each unselected block enters the shared softmax as one slot with logit `q·k̄_b + log n_b + ½σ²_b‖q‖²` and value v̄_b — and use that same variance-corrected expected-mass score to select which blocks get exact attention.

**Non-trivial crux:** The second-moment (Jensen-gap) correction is doing double duty: it calibrates the softmax denominator to conserve dropped attention mass, and it is the only cheap block statistic that makes a mean-pooled score needle-sensitive — unifying Quest-style spike detection and diffuse-evidence retention in a single scalar per block.

# Long-Context Inference-Time Sparse Attention

## Research Question
Design a **sparse attention module** that drops into a pretrained 1.4B-param
causal LLM at inference time and preserves long-context task quality under a
fixed sparsity budget — no retraining, no fine-tuning, no architectural
surgery beyond replacing the attention forward.

## Background
Inference-time sparse attention has been studied along two axes:
**static patterns** (sliding-window, sink + window, BigBird block-sparse,
dilated) and **content-adaptive patterns** (Reformer LSH, NSA-style block-
top-K, Quest). KV-cache compression methods (H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM)
are designed for autoregressive decode with a mutable KV cache and are not
evaluated here — this benchmark uses a parallel-forward setup where every
forward processes the full prefix in one shot and the same `SparseAttention`
module replays at every generation step. Methods whose importance signal
shifts with the observation window (H2O, SnapKV) drift during generation
under this setting; we therefore restrict the baseline set to methods that
operate correctly under parallel forward.

NIAH retrieval and LongBench QA evaluations need instruction-following
ability, so this task uses an instruction-tuned backbone rather than a
base model.

The agent's `SparseAttention` instance (one per attention layer) is
monkey-patched into `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` (12 query heads, 2 KV
heads — the harness handles GQA replication so this module sees 12 heads

"""Inference-time sparse attention module (agent-editable).

Single class ``SparseAttention`` is monkey-patched into Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
by the harness, which calls ``forward(q, k, v, is_causal=True, scale=...)``
once per attention layer (q/k/v already shaped (B, H, N, D), GQA replicated).
The harness reads ``self.last_density`` after every forward and aborts if
density > 0.25 (small slack), except for the dense reference baseline.

PERFORMANCE — read this before redesigning forward(). At N=8192 a naïve
``einsum + softmax + einsum`` materializes a 3 GB bf16 attention matrix per
layer per head and is *slower than dense*. To make sparse actually faster:

  1. Use fused SDPA: ``F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=
     bool_mask, ...)`` is 5–10× faster than einsum + manual softmax.
  2. Cache the mask across layers — it depends only on (N, pattern), not
     q/k/v values, so build once per prompt and reuse across all 24 layers.
  3. For low density (≤ 10%), use ``torch.nn.attention.flex_attention`` with
     ``create_block_mask`` — it compiles a true block-sparse kernel that
     skips entire blocks (PyTorch-native, no Triton-by-hand needed).
  4. Stay in bf16 — fused SDPA handles numerics safely; fp32 upcast 2×s memory.
"""

import math

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EDITABLE REGION START — design the inference-time sparse attention here.
# Lines 31-103 are agent-editable. Everything outside this region is FIXED.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════


class SparseAttention(nn.Module):
    """Foveated, mass-conserving block-sparse attention.

    Exact attention over {sink, local, top-K} KV blocks selected by a
    variance-corrected expected-mass score; every remaining causally
    complete block enters the SAME softmax as one moment-matched
    "phantom" slot with logit  s*q.kbar_b + log n_b + 0.5*s^2*sigma2_b*|q|^2
    and value vbar_b (block value centroid).
    """

    def __init__(self, head_dim, num_heads, block_size=64, density_budget=0.25):
        super().__init__()
        self.head_dim = head_dim
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.block_size = block_size if block_size else 64
        self.density_budget = density_budget
        self.exact_budget = 0.235      # exact-block share; phantoms add ~0.012
        self.q_chunk = 2048            # query-row chunk for memory control
        self.last_density = None

    @torch.no_grad()
    def forward(self, q, k, v, is_causal=False, scale=None):
        B, H, N, D = q.shape
        Bk = self.block_size
        scale = scale if scale is not None else 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)
        dev = q.device
        nb = (N + Bk - 1) // Bk
        pad = nb * Bk - N
        qf, kf, vf = q.float(), k.float(), v.float()
        kp = F.pad(kf, (0, 0, 0, pad)) if pad else kf
        vp = F.pad(vf, (0, 0, 0, pad)) if pad else vf
        qp = F.pad(qf, (0, 0, 0, pad)) if pad else qf
        cnt = torch.full((nb,), float(Bk), device=dev)
        cnt[-1] = float(N - (nb - 1) * Bk)
        c1 = cnt.view(1, 1, nb, 1)
        kb = kp.view(B, H, nb, Bk, D)
        k_mean = kb.sum(3) / c1                                    # (B,H,nb,D)
        sig2 = (kb.pow(2).sum(3) / c1 - k_mean.pow(2)).clamp_min(0).mean(-1)
        v_mean = vp.view(B, H, nb, Bk, D).sum(3) / c1
        logn = cnt.log()
        qn2 = qf.pow(2).sum(-1)                                    # (B,H,N)
        q_mean = qp.view(B, H, nb, Bk, D).sum(3) / c1
        qn2_blk = (F.pad(qn2, (0, pad)) if pad else qn2).view(B, H, nb, Bk).sum(-1) / cnt

        # Block-selection score = mean phantom logit over the query block.
        S = scale * torch.matmul(q_mean, k_mean.transpose(-2, -1))
        S = S + logn.view(1, 1, 1, nb) \
            + (0.5 * scale * scale * sig2.unsqueeze(2) * qn2_blk.unsqueeze(-1)).clamp(max=1.5)
        bi = torch.arange(nb, device=dev)
        causal_blk = bi.view(-1, 1) >= bi.view(1, -1)
        S = S.masked_fill(~causal_blk, float('-inf'))
        # Exact-block count per query block from the causal-density quadratic.
        disc = max(0.0, (2 * nb + 1) ** 2 - 4 * self.exact_budget * nb * (nb + 1))
        K_top = max(1, min(nb, int(((2 * nb + 1) - math.sqrt(disc)) / 2)))
        forced = bi.view(-1, 1) == bi.view(1, -1)                  # diagonal
        if K_top >= 2:
            forced = forced | (bi.view(1, -1) == 0)                # sink block
        if K_top >= 3:
            forced = forced | ((bi.view(-1, 1) - 1) == bi.view(1, -1))  # local
        S = S.masked_fill(forced & causal_blk, float('inf'))
        sel = S.topk(K_top, dim=-1).indices
        block_keep = torch.zeros(B, H, nb, nb, dtype=torch.bool, device=dev)
        block_keep.scatter_(-1, sel, True)
        block_keep &= causal_blk
        block_keep |= bi.view(-1, 1) == bi.view(1, -1)             # diag always exact
        ph_act = (bi.view(-1, 1) > bi.view(1, -1)) & ~block_keep   # (B,H,nb,nb)

        # Density: exact (q,k) pairs analytically + one pair per phantom slot.
        strict = bi.view(-1, 1) > bi.view(1, -1)
        cross = cnt.view(-1, 1) * cnt.view(1, -1)
        exact_pairs = ((block_keep & strict).float() * cross).sum() / (B * H)
        exact_pairs = exact_pairs + (cnt * (cnt + 1) / 2).sum()
        ph_pairs = (ph_act.float().sum(-1) * cnt).sum() / (B * H)
        denom = N * (N + 1) / 2.0
        self.last_density = float((exact_pairs + ph_pairs).item()) / denom

        out = torch.empty_like(qf)
        col = torch.arange(N, device=dev)
        colb = col // Bk
        sig_row = 0.5 * scale * scale * sig2                       # (B,H,nb)
        for i0 in range(0, N, self.q_chunk):
            i1 = min(N, i0 + self.q_chunk)
            rows = torch.arange(i0, i1, device=dev)
            rb = rows // Bk
            le = scale * torch.matmul(qf[:, :, i0:i1], kf.transpose(-2, -1))
            keep = block_keep[:, :, rb, :][..., colb] & (col.view(1, -1) <= rows.view(-1, 1))
            le.masked_fill_(~keep, float('-inf'))
            lp = scale * torch.matmul(qf[:, :, i0:i1], k_mean.transpose(-2, -1))
            lp = lp + logn.view(1, 1, 1, nb) \
                + (sig_row.unsqueeze(2) * qn2[:, :, i0:i1].unsqueeze(-1)).clamp(max=0.5)
            lp = lp.masked_fill(~ph_act[:, :, rb, :], float('-inf'))
            p = torch.softmax(torch.cat([le, lp], dim=-1), dim=-1)
            out[:, :, i0:i1] = torch.matmul(p[..., :N], vf) + torch.matmul(p[..., N:], v_mean)
            del le, lp, p, keep
        return out.to(q.dtype)


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EDITABLE REGION END
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Research proposal — implement THIS idea (provided by the caller)

## Thinking it through

**Step 1 — What does every existing sparse method get wrong in the same way?**

Sliding-window, Quest, block-top-K all share one silent failure mode: whatever isn't selected is treated as if it *doesn't exist*. The softmax renormalizes over the survivors. Two distortions follow:

1. **Denominator lie.** In the dense model, a needle key at 8K wins attention *against* thousands of weak competitors. Drop the competitors and every surviving key's weight is inflated; the output distribution over values shifts away from what the pretrained residual stream expects. QA F1 suffers because diffuse "background evidence" mass — small per token, large in aggregate — is deleted, not approximated.

2. **Selection criterion mismatch.** Quest scores a block by a max-style upper bound (great for needles, systematically over-selects spiky junk blocks); mean-pooled scoring (great for QA-style diffuse evidence) *misses* needles, because one hot key vanishes into the block mean. Nobody's block score captures both regimes.

**Step 2 — The reframe.** Under the budget, we don't have to choose between "attend exactly" and "delete." There's a third state: **attend coarsely**. Every unselected block can be collapsed into a single *phantom token* that participates in the *same* softmax as the exact tokens. Cost: one extra slot per block, ~n/64 — statistically free against a 0.25 density budget.

**Step 3 — The crux: what logit do you give a phantom token?** The naive choice, `q·k̄_b` (attend to the block-mean key), is wrong in a precise, fixable way. We want the phantom to carry the block's *total* softmax mass: Σᵢ exp(s·q·kᵢ). Model the within-block dot products as Gaussian, q·kᵢ ~ N(q·k̄_b, q᷐Cᵦq), approximate the quadratic form isotropically with a cached scalar σ²_b = mean per-dim key variance, and the moment-generating function gives:

**ℓ_b = s·q·k̄_b + log n_b + ½·s²·σ²_b·‖q‖²**,  phantom value = v̄_b.

Three terms, three jobs: mean similarity, block size (mass conservation), and a **Jensen-gap variance correction**. That last term is the payoff:

- It makes the phantom mass a *calibrated* estimate of the dropped mass → the denominator is honest, exact-block weights match dense-model attention scale. Fixes distortion (1).
- Now use **the same ℓ_b as the block-selection score** (top-K blocks per head per query-block by ℓ_b). A block containing one needle key has huge σ²_b — the variance term flags it even though the mean hides it. A block of uniformly moderate evidence has high mean term. One scalar handles both regimes. Fixes distortion (2), replacing Quest's loose max-bound with an expected-mass criterion that is budget-optimal in the "capture the most attention mass exactly" sense.

**Step 4 — Assembly (Foveated, Mass-Conserving Sparse Attention):**

- Per forward, per KV block b: cache k̄_b, v̄_b, n_b, σ²_b — one O(n) pass.
- Per query block: exact attention over {sink block, 2 diagonal/local blocks, top-K blocks by ℓ_b} spending ~0.23 density; **concatenate phantom logits ℓ_b for all remaining causally-complete blocks** (strictly below the diagonal query block; partial block is covered by the exact local band) and their values v̄_b; run **one softmax over exact + phantom slots**. Output = exact-weighted values + phantom-weighted centroid values.
- Replays identically at every generation step (fully recomputed from q,k,v, no mutable state), so it's drift-free under the parallel-forward protocol. GQA replication is handled upstream; per-head top-K naturally lets retrieval heads and local heads pick different blocks.

Why this beats the baselines specifically here: on **niah_8k**, the variance term guarantees needle-block selection *and* the honest denominator keeps the needle's attention weight at its dense-model value rather than an inflated one (important when the model must copy the needle verbatim). On **Qasper/MultiFieldQA**, the phantom background preserves the aggregate contribution of thousands of weakly-relevant tokens that hard-sparse methods amputate — the residual stream sees an input statistically close to dense attention's, which is exactly what "no retraining" demands.

**Core idea:** Replace hard block deletion with moment-matched phantom tokens — each unselected block enters the shared softmax as one slot with logit `q·k̄_b + log n_b + ½σ²_b‖q‖²` and value v̄_b — and use that same variance-corrected expected-mass score to select which blocks get exact attention.

**Non-trivial crux:** The second-moment (Jensen-gap) correction is doing double duty: it calibrates the softmax denominator to conserve dropped attention mass, and it is the only cheap block statistic that makes a mean-pooled score needle-sensitive — unifying Quest-style spike detection and diffuse-evidence retention in a single scalar per block.

## Research Question
Design a **sparse attention module** that drops into a pretrained 1.4B-param
causal LLM at inference time and preserves long-context task quality under a
fixed sparsity budget — no retraining, no fine-tuning, no architectural
surgery beyond replacing the attention forward.

Inference-time sparse attention has been studied along two axes:
**static patterns** (sliding-window, sink + window, BigBird block-sparse,
dilated) and **content-adaptive patterns** (Reformer LSH, NSA-style block-
top-K, Quest). KV-cache compression methods (H2O, SnapKV, StreamingLLM)
are designed for autoregressive decode with a mutable KV cache and are not
evaluated here — this benchmark uses a parallel-forward setup where every
forward processes the full prefix in one shot and the same `SparseAttention`
module replays at every generation step. Methods whose importance signal
shifts with the observation window (H2O, SnapKV) drift during generation
under this setting; we therefore restrict the baseline set to methods that
operate correctly under parallel forward.

NIAH retrieval and LongBench QA evaluations need instruction-following
ability, so this task uses an instruction-tuned backbone rather than a
base model.
